# Vision acceptance fixtures

These six PNG pairs are deterministic, project-created fixtures generated by
`node tools/generate-vision-fixtures.mjs`:

| Fixture | Class | Intended condition |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `humanoid-pencil-faint` | humanoid | low-contrast graphite-like drawing |
| `humanoid-colored` | humanoid | colored marker drawing |
| `humanoid-shadow` | humanoid | warm paper with dark uneven ink |
| `humanoid-nonideal` | humanoid | asymmetric limbs and imperfect proportions |
| `nonhumanoid-cat` | nonhumanoid | animal silhouette |
| `nonhumanoid-rocket` | nonhumanoid | object silhouette |

The source PNGs contain a warm paper gradient and deterministic sensor-like noise
outside the drawing. Each `.golden.png` is an annotated binary silhouette with a
small two-pixel edge tolerance for the classical morphology step. It is not an
output captured from `segment()`; changing the algorithm does not regenerate
these files unless the intended drawing annotation itself changes.

`fixtures.test.ts` decodes the RGBA PNGs without a runtime image library, runs the
real typed-array `segment()` implementation, and checks IoU (≥0.90 for all four
humanoid fixtures and ≥0.60 for both nonhumanoid fixtures). The same humanoid
annotations feed the rig tests. `tests/fixtures/rigs/` contains four serialized
rig goldens; tests compare mesh/weight structure, sampled numeric values, schema
fields available on this branch, and a 1-second-per-fixture build budget.

These are synthetic photo-like acceptance inputs, not photographs of children.
They cover image-processing behavior while keeping CI reproducible and free of
personal media. Manual visual review of the mask-editor canvas and device camera
capture remains a separate Issue 9/14 acceptance item.
